_what_this_is: A node type is a REQUIRED PATTERN OF TYPED, DIRECTED PATHS that a node either matches or does not. It is not a label somebody applied. The content of a node does not decide its type; its paths do.
judgment: Judgment does not disappear. Somebody still decided that a control must be enforced from outside the grant. What changes is where that decision lives: out of a classifier's head and into a formula that is visible, versioned, inspectable and arguable.
not_a_node: A score is not a node and there is no edge to one. Not a rating, not a risk level, not a severity. Adding one would not be a modelling choice, it would be a verdict, and the same ABP is dangerous in one deployment and harmless in the next. The risk work above this holds the assets, and that is where a score can exist.
universes: Each type names the universe it belongs to, which is a modelling decision made once in universes.py and checked by the gate: a type with no universe is a node nobody owns.

node_types.name: Verb
node_types.is: The action half of a primitive, on its own.
node_types.formula: [Verb] := a node that is the -verb_of-> at least one [Capability]
node_types.note: A verb with no capability under it is a word, not a node in this graph.

node_types.name: ObjectClass
node_types.formula: [ObjectClass] := a node that is -acted_on_by-> at least one [Capability]

node_types.name: ReachClass
node_types.formula: [ReachClass] := a node that is -reachable_from-> at least one [Capability]
node_types.note: What host, tenant and world MEAN is the deployment shape's to say, not the grammar's, which is why a reach class node carries the shapes that name it rather than a definition.

node_types.name: Family
node_types.is: A grouping of primitives for a reader.
node_types.formula: [Family] := a node that is the -family_of-> at least one [Capability]
node_types.note: A family is an altitude device: it groups facts for a reader and carries none of its own.

node_types.name: Capability
node_types.formula: [Capability] := a node with a -has_verb-> [Verb] and an -acts_on-> [ObjectClass] and a -reaches-> [ReachClass]
node_types.note: All three, or it is not a primitive. A specific path, host or mailbox is an INSTANCE of a primitive and never a new one.

node_types.name: DeploymentShape
node_types.formula: [DeploymentShape] := a node that -grants-> at least one [Capability]
node_types.note: Not a product. Two shapes here are the same product with one setting different.

node_types.name: GrantedCapability
node_types.is: A capability in a particular shape's grant.
node_types.formula: [GrantedCapability] := a [Capability] with an inbound -grants-> from a [DeploymentShape], carrying a -bounded_by-> [Barrier] and a -known_by-> [EvidenceTier]
node_types.note: THE NODE THAT CARRIES THE BARRIER. The barrier is a property of the capability IN A SHAPE, never of the capability itself, which is the whole reason the ABP is about the deployment rather than the product.

node_types.name: Barrier
node_types.is: What stands between the agent and a capability.
node_types.formula: [Barrier] := a node that -bounds-> at least one [GrantedCapability]

node_types.name: Control
node_types.is: A barrier that actually bounds anything.
node_types.formula: [Control] := a [Barrier] that is -enforced_by-> an [Enforcer] the [Grant] does not include
node_types.note: THE ENFORCER TEST, AS A FORMULA RATHER THAN A FIELD. Until v0.3.0 this was `is_control: true' on a barrier, which is a label somebody applied. Now it is a path pattern, so you can disagree with the classification by pointing at a line. Exactly one of the four barriers matches, and the site fails to build if that stops being true.

node_types.name: Mandate
node_types.formula: [Mandate] := a node that -authorises-> at least one [Capability]

node_types.name: Excess
node_types.formula: [Excess] := a [GrantedCapability] with NO -authorised_by-> path to the [Mandate] in scope
node_types.note: A capability the mandate never mentioned was not authorised. Unstated is not permission.

node_types.name: UnboundedExcess
node_types.note: The only number on the label a buyer can move. Every control bought moves one capability into the fourth barrier and the count falls by one.

node_types.name: Shortfall
node_types.formula: [Shortfall] := a [Capability] that a [Mandate] -authorises-> and no [DeploymentShape] in scope -grants->

node_types.name: Product
node_types.is: A vendor's product, which is not a shape.
node_types.formula: [Product] := a node that -has_variant-> at least one [DeploymentShape]
node_types.note: The ABP is about the deployment, not the product. A product is the node two shapes share when they differ by one setting, and nothing on this site is a claim about one.

node_types.name: Tool
node_types.is: What a shape reaches a capability through.
node_types.formula: [Tool] := a node that a [DeploymentShape] -runs_with-> and that -exposes-> at least one [Capability]
node_types.note: In the vendor's own words: shell (Bash), the assistant's Gmail connector, REST API: workflows. A tool that exposes nothing is a name and not a node here.

node_types.name: Scope
node_types.is: A vendor's own identifier for what a consent permits.
node_types.formula: [Scope] := a node that a [DeploymentShape] is -scoped_by-> and that -permits-> at least one [Capability]
node_types.note: In the vendor's word, never translated: gmail.readonly is the node, and what it permits is the edge. The connector shapes contributed by riskmandate.ai reach most of their rows this way.

node_types.name: Setting
node_types.formula: [Setting] := a node that -narrows-> at least one [Capability] and -moves-> it to at least one [Barrier]
node_types.note: Two kinds today, both from published data: the reduction the map publishes per capability, and the setting that distinguishes two variants of one product, derived by diffing their grants. The confirmations flag is the second kind.

provenance.note: The formulas are run against the graph on every build and the `matched` counts are the result, not fields anybody set.
